# Working in this repository {.unnumbered}

This book is for people who write content for the course fork of *Think Python* (3rd edition) at
<https://github.com/y-rosenthal/yrThinkPython>. The fork's website is
<https://y-rosenthal.github.io/yrThinkPython/>.

**Each rule has one place in the repository, and this book shows those places.** This page holds what is not
in the repository's files: how to set up your computer, and the workflow of a content author. The next
chapters are the rule files themselves, included as they are, so this book is never out of step with them:

| Chapter | The file it includes | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| The repository | `README.md` | The layout, how the website is published, how the fork follows Downey's book |
| Editing the Think Python notebooks | `.claude/skills/notebook-conventions/SKILL.md` | The rules for the chapter notebooks and the suggested solutions |
| Add a page to the book | `.claude/skills/add-page/SKILL.md` | How a new chapter or page gets into the book |
| Prof. Rosenthal's course additions | `yr/README.md` | The rules for the course's pages: the additions pages, the review pages, their format, style, tools and procedures |

Links in these chapters are relative to the repository, not to this book: open the file on GitHub when a
link does not work here. `AGENTS.md` holds the rules for AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot
and others) and lists the skills in `.claude/skills/`; you can ask Claude Code in your own words, or type a skill's
name. An agent other than Claude Code can follow a skill: tell it to read `.claude/skills/NAME/SKILL.md`.

To build this book:

```bash
cd author-guide
quarto render          # the HTML goes to author-guide/_book/ (not committed)
quarto preview         # or: open a live preview in the browser
```

## Set up your computer

You need Linux or macOS, `git`, and Python 3.12 at `/usr/bin/python3`. The tools create the rest:

- **The book's venv**, `~/.venvs/yrThinkPython`. The build scripts create it the first time.
  The repository is in Dropbox, so the venv is outside it.
- **The Colab-like kernel**, `~/.venvs/colablike`. `yr/tools/review.sh` creates it the first
  time you run `sync` or `check`. It has the same Python, IPython and ipykernel versions as Colab.
  The tools write the stored outputs of the review pages with this kernel only, so the pages look the same as
  in Colab.
- **`uv`**, the tool that builds the Colab-like kernel. `review.sh` installs it into the book's
  venv if it is missing.
- **Quarto**, only to build this book.

Run all commands from the root folder of the repository.

## The workflow: branch, check, publish

Every push to the branch `v3` publishes the website. Thus:

1. Make a topic branch before you change anything:

   ```bash
   git switch v3
   git pull
   git switch -c my-topic
   ```

2. Make your changes, and run the checks that the rule file for your task names (for a review page:
   `review.sh sync` and `review.sh check`; for a chapter or an additions page: `run_notebooks.sh`).
3. Always run the fast check of all notebooks:

   ```bash
   python3 .claude/skills/check-notebooks/check_notebooks.py
   ```

4. Build the website on your computer, and look at the pages you changed:

   ```bash
   .claude/skills/build-book/build_book.sh
   ```

   The output is in `jb/_build/html/`. The script must say "no new warnings".
5. Commit, and push your branch.
6. To publish, merge the branch into `v3` and push `v3`. The `yrpublish` skill of Claude Code does
   all the checks, the merge, the push and a check of the live site.

The deploy workflow (`.github/workflows/deploy-book.yml`) runs `check_notebooks.py` first. If it
finds a problem, the website does not change.

**Corrections to the book itself** go to Allen Downey as a GitHub issue, not as a pull request.
The `contribute-upstream` skill writes the issue text. **Updates from Allen Downey** come in with the
`sync-upstream` skill (the chapter "The repository", "Keeping up with the original").

### Students see the new version without a reload

After you publish, students do not need to reload a page to see the new version. `jb/_static/yr.js`,
which every page of the website loads (also pages that you add later), checks for a new version 3
seconds after a page opens, every 5 minutes while the page is on the screen, and each time the student
comes back to its tab:

- When the student comes back to a tab with an old version, the page reloads, at the same place.
- While the student looks at a page, a bar at the top says "A new version of this website was
  published", with a **Reload** button.

GitHub Pages gives each page a new date on every publish. So after a publish, the bar can also come on
a page that did not change. A notebook that a student saved in Google Drive (**File > Save a copy in
Drive**) does not change: to get the new version, the student opens the page again from the website.

## Tools reference

Every tool takes `-h` or `--help`, which prints what the tool does and its options. For example,
`yr/tools/review.sh sync --help` or `.claude/skills/build-book/build_book.sh --help`. The review-page tools are
listed in the chapter "Prof. Rosenthal's course additions", "Tools"; the others:

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `python3 .claude/skills/check-notebooks/check_notebooks.py` | Fast check of all notebooks (its `--help` lists the checks) |
| `.claude/skills/check-notebooks/run_notebooks.sh chapters/chapNN.ipynb` | Runs a chapter or an additions page |
| `.claude/skills/build-book/build_book.sh` | Builds the website on your computer |
| `python3 .claude/skills/yrpublish/verify_live.py` | Checks the live website |
| `python3 .claude/skills/notebook-conventions/nb_cells.py NOTEBOOK` | Lists the cells of a notebook |
